question: What cultural belief often causes many communities to tolerate domestic violence?

options.A: Immediate community intervention during family disputes
options.B: Universal access to legal education for all citizens
options.C: Equal economic power sharing between men and women
options.D: Normalization of patriarchal dominance and domestic discipline

explanation: You're doing great! In many places, old-school cultural norms wrongly frame male control and physical correction as normal or acceptable. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

options.A: Conducting annual financial audits for human resources
options.B: Designing new production machinery to eliminate safety hazards
options.C: Coordinating medical treatments and return-to-work plans for injured staff
options.D: Purchasing personal protective equipment for the entire industrial plant

explanation: Exactly! As case managers, nurses guide injured workers through their recovery and help them safely get back to work. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h2)

question: Which mental health challenge is very common among young brides who are cut off from their friends?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Schizophrenic hallucinations
options.C: Depression and anxiety
options.D: Obsessive compulsive rituals

explanation: Loneliness, losing their childhood, and heavy adult responsibilities often trigger deep depression and anxiety in young wives. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h5)

question: What actually happens inside the body during a Type I allergic reaction to a medication?

options.A: Accumulation of fluid in the peripheral blood vessels
options.B: Mast cell degranulation releasing histamine and other mediators
options.C: Direct toxicity of the drug on the kidney tubules
options.D: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells in the liver

explanation: When antibodies trigger mast cells to burst open and release histamine, it leads to rapid itching, swelling, and trouble breathing. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is family planning counseling a must before a patient is discharged from PAC?

options.A: It helps prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and repeat abortions
options.B: It satisfies legal requirements for hospital record keeping
options.C: It determines the exact gestational age of the previous pregnancy
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of postpartum depression

explanation: You'll learn in practice that fertility can return very quickly after an abortion. Giving contraceptive counseling right away empowers your patient to space or prevent future pregnancies safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: Why is it important for assisted living homes to balance safety rules with personal freedom?

options.A: Residents who experience freedom no longer require medical care.
options.B: Federal laws prohibit any facility from locking doors or windows.
options.C: Excessive rules can strip away a resident's dignity and sense of home.
options.D: Safety protocols have no impact on the mental health of older adults.

explanation: You've got this! Safety matters, but making a home feel like a strict prison hurts residents' happiness and takes away their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is patient stability so important when deciding whether or not to delegate a task?

options.A: Stable patients do not require any monitoring from healthcare workers
options.B: Unstable patients always pay more for hospital accommodation
options.C: Stable patients are harder to communicate with than unstable ones
options.D: Unstable patients require continuous clinical judgment that only a registered nurse can provide

explanation: When a patient's condition can change rapidly, it needs a professional nurse's close assessment rather than auxiliary care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: What should you do immediately after using a needle to draw blood?

options.A: Carefully scoop the needle cap back on using one hand to prevent injury
options.B: Place the needle on a clean tray until the end of the shift
options.C: Break the needle tip off with forceps before throwing it in the bin
options.D: Drop the unrecapped needle directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container

explanation: Never recap needles! Dropping them straight into the sharps box right beside you is the safest way to avoid accidental needle-pricks. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is a key part of emergency preparedness in a home care plan?

options.A: Disconnecting all medical equipment to save electricity
options.B: Waiting for the annual checkup to report severe symptoms
options.C: Knowing who to call and what steps to take during a sudden crisis
options.D: Relying solely on neighbors for medical decisions

explanation: When an emergency strikes, panic shouldn't take over. Having a clear plan of who to call keeps both the patient and family safe. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which organ needs routine blood test monitoring when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?

options.A: Thyroid
options.B: Heart
options.C: Lungs
options.D: Liver

explanation: Azole drugs are processed by the liver, so we keep an eye on liver enzymes during long-term therapy to catch any stress early. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h7)

question: When would a nurse most likely need to insert a flatus tube?

options.A: Chronic diarrhea lasting longer than three days
options.B: Severe postoperative gaseous abdominal distention
options.C: A suspected complete mechanical bowel obstruction
options.D: Active and profuse upper gastrointestinal bleeding

explanation: Flatus tubes are super helpful when gas builds up painfully after surgery because the bowels are temporarily slow. Spot on! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is the common medical term for a nosebleed originating from the anterior nasal septum?

options.A: Rhinorrhea
options.B: Anosmia
options.C: Epistaxis
options.D: Sinusitis

explanation: Epistaxis is the clinical term for bleeding from the blood vessels inside the nasal cavity. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h7)

question: How does a rigid professional hierarchy negatively impact patient safety?

options.A: Patients refuse to take their prescribed hospital medicines
options.B: Pharmacists stop checking the expiry dates on drugs
options.C: Doctors are forced to do all the nursing paperwork themselves
options.D: Junior staff may stay silent even when they spot a dangerous error

explanation: Exactly. When junior staff are too scared to speak up due to intimidation, dangerous mistakes can slip right through and harm the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h6)

question: Which of these examples shows a positive feedback mechanism in the body?

options.A: Thyroid hormone stopping TSH release from the anterior pituitary
options.B: Parathyroid hormone raising low blood calcium back to normal
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Insulin lowering blood glucose levels after a meal is eaten

explanation: Positive feedback pushes a process forward until a goal is reached! During childbirth, contractions release oxytocin, which causes even stronger contractions until the baby arrives. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the gold-standard laboratory test used to confirm an Ebola infection?

options.A: Routine microscopic examination of red blood cells
options.B: X-ray imaging of the chest
options.C: Stool microscopy for parasites
options.D: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)

explanation: Correct! RT-PCR is the reliable test that catches the virus's RNA in blood samples. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h4)

question: What does male sexual dysfunction mainly affect?

options.A: Upper respiratory function
options.B: Physical intimacy and satisfaction
options.C: Renal filtration capacity
options.D: Skeletal muscle development

explanation: You've got this! Male sexual dysfunction simply means there's trouble with enjoying or engaging in sexual activity. It's all about intimacy and satisfaction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h1)

question: Which antiseptic is most commonly used to clean the skin before putting in a cannula?

options.A: Hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Plain tap water
options.C: Chlorhexidine
options.D: Sterile mineral oil

explanation: Chlorhexidine is our go-to skin cleaner for stopping germs and keeping nasty bloodstream infections away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h4)

question: What do we call using someone else's ideas or words without giving them proper credit?

options.A: Synthesis
options.B: Plagiarism
options.C: Citation
options.D: Paraphrasing

explanation: Plagiarism means taking another person's work or ideas and presenting them as your own without acknowledging them. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of vaccinating animals on a large scale in public health?

options.A: To cure animals that are already showing severe clinical signs of illness
options.B: To create a protective barrier that stops pathogens from spreading to humans
options.C: To increase the market weight and commercial value of livestock herds
options.D: To replace human vaccination schedules with veterinary immunization protocols

explanation: Exactly! Vaccinating animals keeps them healthy and stops zoonotic diseases from jumping over to humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the everyday medical name for the outer, visible part of the ear?

options.A: Eustachian tube
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Auricle
options.D: Cochlea

explanation: Great job! The auricle (or pinna) is shaped just right to catch sounds and funnel them down into the ear canal. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h2)

question: What does 'cumulative frequency' actually mean in a nursing data set?

options.A: The exact average of the highest and lowest scores
options.B: The percentage of missing records in a study
options.C: The difference between two separate patient groups
options.D: A running total of frequencies added up row by row

explanation: Think of it like adding coins to a piggy bank step by step—cumulative frequency is just the running total! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why do older adults with sensory loss often start withdrawing from social activities?

options.A: Difficulty with communication and environmental interaction creates frustration
options.B: Physical fatigue caused by overworking the remaining healthy senses
options.C: Mandatory medical quarantine protocols for sensory impairment
options.D: A sudden loss of interest in hobbies and personal relationships

explanation: Think about it: when it's exhausting just to hear what people are saying or navigate a room, socializing stops being fun and starts feeling like hard work. Patience and empathy go a long way here! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h1)

question: How does chemoprophylaxis differ from standard immunization?

options.A: Chemoprophylaxis cures chronic illnesses, while immunization is only used for acute emergency surgeries.
options.B: Chemoprophylaxis creates lifelong immunity, whereas vaccines wear off after a single week.
options.C: Immunization is given to animals only, whereas chemoprophylaxis is exclusively reserved for human patients.
options.D: Chemoprophylaxis uses medications to prevent infection, whereas immunization uses antigens to stimulate antibody production.

explanation: You've got this! Chemoprophylaxis means using protective drugs (like malaria prevention tablets), while vaccines train your body's own immune system to fight back. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h5)

question: Which of these is a GOOD practice that actually protects a DRF, rather than harming it?

options.A: Bureaucratic delays in government procurement processes
options.B: Strict adherence to the FEFO inventory system
options.C: Political pressure to give out un-reimbursed free drugs
options.D: Internal staff pilferage and unauthorized drug taking

explanation: You've got this! FEFO is a smart safety habit. The other options (delays, theft, giving away free drugs) are threats that kill the fund. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h6)

question: When checking lab results, which finding usually tells you the patient's body is actively fighting off an infection?

options.A: Low platelet concentration levels
options.B: Reduced blood urea nitrogen
options.C: Elevated white blood cell count
options.D: Decreased red blood cell count

explanation: You got it! A high white blood cell count (leukocytosis) means the bone marrow is pumping out extra soldiers to tackle invading germs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which blood test measures general inflammation by checking how fast red blood cells settle?

options.A: Liver function test
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Complete blood cell count
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: Often called ESR, this test watches how quickly red blood cells drop to the bottom of a test tube. Faster settling usually means high inflammation in the body. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h5)

question: What physical signs are most typical of an acute gout flare in a joint?

options.A: Slow, painless swelling that develops over several months
options.B: Intense redness, extreme tenderness, and localized heat
options.C: Visible shortening of the limb and muscle atrophy
options.D: Cool, pale skin with complete numbness and no pain

explanation: When gout flares up, the joint gets super angry—it turns bright red, feels very hot to the touch, and hurts so much you can barely let anyone look at it. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h5)

question: What valve does blood pass through immediately after leaving the right ventricle?

options.A: Mitral valve
options.B: Aortic semilunar valve
options.C: Pulmonary semilunar valve
options.D: Tricuspid valve

explanation: As the right ventricle contracts, blood pushes open the pulmonary semilunar valve to enter the pulmonary trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which heart chamber grows thicker and more muscular in the weeks after birth because of its new workload?

options.A: Right ventricle
options.B: Right atrium
options.C: Left ventricle
options.D: Left atrium

explanation: Fantastic! Because the left ventricle is now pumping blood through the entire body without the placenta's help, its muscle works harder and naturally grows thicker over time. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h6)

question: How does task-shifting help improve healthcare in understaffed rural areas?

options.A: By moving specialist obstetricians to every village clinic in the country
options.B: By transferring pregnant patients to urban centers permanently
options.C: By replacing all nurses with automated computer systems
options.D: By training community health workers to safely deliver certain basic health interventions

explanation: You nailed it! Task-shifting bridges the staff gap by letting trained community workers handle basic, safe tasks when professional nurses aren't enough. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h8)

question: If a patient has severe hypertension, which symptom might they complain about?

options.A: Severe pain in the lower abdomen
options.B: Morning occipital headaches
options.C: Sudden swelling in both feet
options.D: Uncontrolled trembling of hands

explanation: A pounding headache right at the back of the head (occipital area) when waking up is a classic warning sign of very high pressure. Keep storing these clinical pearls! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h3)

question: During a disease outbreak, which of these is a core duty for a community health nurse?

options.A: Writing national health policies and approving federal budgets
options.B: Isolating entire towns by deploying armed security forces
options.C: Conducting contact tracing and educating community members on prevention
options.D: Manufacturing vaccines inside local primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! Nurses are right on the frontline—tracking down contacts, teaching families how to stay safe, and helping at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h8)

question: Why is uncovering hidden health needs an important goal of community diagnosis?

options.A: Doctors refuse to treat patients who walk into the clinic
options.B: Hospital records always contain complete and flawless data
options.C: Many sick people stay at home and never visit a health facility
options.D: Government officials order nurses to hide serious diseases

explanation: Hospital registries only capture those who manage to reach the clinic, leaving out vulnerable people suffering in silence at home. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h2)

question: A stroke patient is struggling with swallowing food safely and speaking clearly. Who should the nurse call for help?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Social worker
options.C: Prosthetist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at helping patients overcome both communication hurdles and swallowing issues (dysphagia). [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h4)

question: What type of energy do infrared thermometers pick up from the human body?

options.A: Sound wave echoes
options.B: Electrical current
options.C: Ultraviolet radiation
options.D: Infrared radiation

explanation: These thermometers are built to sense the invisible heat energy that naturally radiates from warm human skin. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: Why is a baby with neonatal tetanus at high risk for aspiration pneumonia?

options.A: Swallowing difficulties and tube feeding increase risk
options.B: High fever melts the protective airway mucus
options.C: The bacterial toxin directly attacks lung tissue
options.D: The lungs produce excessive fluid naturally

explanation: Spot on! Because they cannot swallow normally and rely on tube feeding, it is much easier for fluids or milk to accidentally enter the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h7)

question: What is the main problem in the body that causes diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Defects in insulin production or action
options.B: Overproduction of digestive enzymes
options.C: Excessive secretion of glucagon
options.D: Rapid breakdown of thyroid hormones

explanation: Think of diabetes as a trouble with insulin—either the body isn't making enough of it, or it's not using the insulin it has properly, which leaves too much sugar in the blood. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h1)

question: When doing an ear check on an adult using an otoscope, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna) to straighten the canal?

options.A: Tilt the patient's head forward
options.B: Push the tragus inward firmly
options.C: Pull the earlobe straight down
options.D: Pull the pinna up and back

explanation: You've got it! Pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the adult ear canal so you can get a clear view of the eardrum. (For kids, remember you pull down and back!) [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why does a narrow upper airway cause a whistling or high-pitched breathing sound known as stridor?

options.A: The heart valves are clicking against the chest wall
options.B: Blood is rushing too fast through the neck veins
options.C: Mucus is vibrating inside the lower lung tissue
options.D: Air is forced rapidly through a tight, narrowed space

explanation: Stridor sounds a bit like wind whistling through a crack in a door. It happens when air has to squeeze forcefully through a narrowed airway passage. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why does primary health care place heavy emphasis on nutrition and safe water alongside medical treatment?

options.A: Nurses are trained as civil engineers rather than clinicians
options.B: Preventing disease through basic sanitation stops sickness before it starts
options.C: Doctors refuse to treat patients who do not drink boiled water
options.D: Water and food are more profitable than pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Clean water and good nutrition address the root environmental causes of infection, reducing the burden on clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which type of validity involves checking if a new tool compares well with an established gold standard?

options.A: Surface validity
options.B: Criterion validity
options.C: Face validity
options.D: Content validity

explanation: Criterion validity is established when a new instrument scores similarly to a trusted, proven gold-standard tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which of these statements about nursing leadership is FALSE?

options.A: It is built by taking on small projects and precepting students.
options.B: It is a continuous developmental journey throughout a career.
options.C: It can be cultivated through mentorship and continuing education.
options.D: It is an innate trait that cannot be learned or improved over time.

explanation: Leadership isn't a rare magic power you are born with! Anyone can grow and improve their leadership skills over time through practice, learning, and good mentors. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why are AROM exercises great for keeping a patient's nervous system working well?

options.A: They require the brain to send nerve impulses that actively contract the muscles.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any other physical therapy.
options.C: They stop the patient from ever feeling tired during the hospital stay.
options.D: They force the joints to move past their normal anatomical limits safely.

explanation: Spot on! When the patient initiates the move themselves, the communication highway between the brain and muscles stays open and strong. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to advocate for food policy changes?

options.A: They are primarily responsible for writing national agricultural laws
options.B: They witness the direct health impacts of poor nutrition in clinical practice
options.C: They control the financial budgets of international food agencies
options.D: They manage the commercial distribution of imported grain

explanation: Nurses see malnutrition and diet-related disease daily, giving them firsthand evidence of policy needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: What is the term for a surgical emergency where internal organs pop out through an opened surgical wound?

options.A: Ecchymosis
options.B: Dehiscence
options.C: Evisceration
options.D: Maceration

explanation: Evisceration is a scary medical emergency where organs protrude past the incision line. It needs immediate sterile coverage and a surgeon right away! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h8)

question: A patient with suspected Addison's disease is at high risk for which dangerous electrolyte imbalance?

options.A: Hypercalcemia resulting from excess bone breakdown
options.B: Hyperkalemia due to aldosterone deficiency
options.C: Severe hyponatremia caused by water intoxication
options.D: Hypokalemia caused by excessive renal excretion

explanation: Aldosterone is the hormone that normally tells our kidneys to flush out extra potassium. Without enough aldosterone, potassium builds up in the blood, leading to risky high levels (hyperkalemia). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h6)

question: In which lobe of the brain is the primary touch (somatosensory) cortex found?

options.A: Temporal lobe
options.B: Parietal lobe
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: You've got this! The parietal lobe sits right at the top-back of your brain and is the main station for processing everything you touch. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h6)

question: Why do health teams rush to carry out mass immunization campaigns as soon as a new refugee camp opens?

options.A: To prevent rapid outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases in crowded spaces
options.B: To fulfill mandatory international tourism travel requirements
options.C: To permanently cure all existing chronic medical conditions
options.D: To replace the need for clean drinking water and sanitation

explanation: When children are packed closely together in a new camp setting, infectious diseases can spread like wildfire. Quick vaccinations stop epidemics before they start! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Promoting the health and recovery of the patient
options.B: Fulfilling social needs of the nursing staff
options.C: Gathering data for hospital financial records
options.D: Building long-lasting personal friendships

explanation: Unlike normal friendships, professional nursing relationships are purposely designed to focus entirely on helping the patient get better. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why can traditional power dynamics sometimes delay medical care for pregnant women?

options.A: Women are legally banned from talking to doctors first.
options.B: Hospitals refuse to treat women without a signed consent form.
options.C: Men always prefer traditional herbs over modern medicine.
options.D: The woman may need to wait for the man's approval and funds.

explanation: When getting care depends entirely on someone else's permission and money, emergencies can worsen while waiting. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h4)

question: A patient who had a leg amputation complains of severe pain in the toes of the missing foot. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Tell the patient firmly that the foot is gone so it cannot hurt
options.B: Remove the surgical dressing immediately to look for infection
options.C: Acknowledge the pain and administer prescribed medication for phantom limb pain
options.D: Check the remaining leg for signs of a new injury

explanation: Phantom limb sensations and pain are very real neurological events that require validation and appropriate medical treatment. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h5)

question: When is a formative evaluation done during an IEC program?

options.A: While nurses are writing hospital financial reports
options.B: Before the program starts, to test messages and materials
options.C: As an emergency response to a sudden disease outbreak
options.D: Only after all health campaigns have permanently ended

explanation: Think of formative evaluation as 'forming' your plan—you test your posters and messages before launching to make sure they actually make sense to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: Studying a rare medical condition, a researcher asks early patients to connect her with other patients they know. What technique is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Stratified sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: Spot on! Just like a snowball rolls and gets bigger, your participant list grows as each person refers you to the next. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the medical term for when an erection goes away and the penis returns to a soft state?

options.A: Tumescence
options.B: Detumescence
options.C: Vasodilation
options.D: Priapism

explanation: Keep learning! Detumescence simply means the easing of an erection back to normal, soft tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of reflective practice in nursing?

options.A: To punish staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To turn everyday experience into professional growth
options.C: To replace the formal nursing assessment process
options.D: To reduce the paperwork required at shift handover

explanation: Reflective practice allows nurses to learn from past situations and improve future care. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why does Superior Vena Cava Syndrome cause facial swelling?

options.A: Allergic reactions to chemotherapy puff up the face
options.B: Lymph nodes in the neck shrink and pull skin tight
options.C: Blood flow from the head and neck is blocked from reaching the heart
options.D: Fluid retention is caused by failing kidneys

explanation: When a tumor blocks the superior vena cava, blood backs up in the upper body, causing noticeable swelling in the face, neck, and arms. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the main job of dietary fats in infants and toddlers?

options.A: Acting as the main fuel source for red blood cells
options.B: Preventing childhood obesity and sluggishness
options.C: Supporting central nervous system development and brain growth
options.D: Supplying all the necessary vitamin C for the immune system

explanation: Exactly! Little ones need healthy fats because their growing brains and nerves depend heavily on them for proper development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h2)

question: How do vaccines work to protect a child's body against infections?

options.A: By stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
options.B: By coating the stomach lining to block germ absorption
options.C: By increasing the body temperature to kill viruses
options.D: By providing immediate chemical destruction of all bacteria

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines introduce safe, weakened parts of a germ to train the immune system so it knows how to fight back if the real disease ever shows up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h4)

question: Over time, how does chronic, untreated high blood pressure harm the heart?

options.A: By permanently dilating all major veins in the lower extremities
options.B: By thinning the heart muscle walls and causing extreme hypotension
options.C: By eliminating the need for peripheral vascular resistance
options.D: By injuring arterial walls and causing left ventricular hypertrophy

explanation: Fighting against high pressure everyday makes the heart muscle work out too hard—just like lifting heavy weights, it gets bulky and thick (hypertrophy), which isn't good for it long-term. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h5)

question: What term describes the brain's amazing ability to reorganize and form new pathways after an injury?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Osmotic demyelination
options.C: Neuroplasticity
options.D: Cerebrovascular atrophy

explanation: Neuroplasticity means healthy parts of the brain can step up and learn to take over functions lost from damaged areas. The brain is truly resilient! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h8)

question: What does 'participatory governance' mean in primary health care?

options.A: Leaving all health decisions entirely to elected politicians
options.B: Allowing only doctors to vote on clinic budgets
options.C: Involving local community members in health planning and decisions
options.D: Handing over total hospital ownership to private investors

explanation: Spot on! Participatory governance means the community isn't just a receiver of care—they help shape the health services they get. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h4)

question: A community health nurse notices a 12-year-old girl has suddenly stopped coming to school and clinic. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the absence since it falls outside routine clinical nursing duties
options.B: Investigate the reason for absence through a home visit or family talk
options.C: Report the family to the international criminal court immediately
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to see if the child returns on her own

explanation: That's right! A sudden dropout is a red flag. Checking in with the family helps you find out what's going on and offer support early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h4)

question: What part of the fibrous tunic is completely clear to let light pass into the eye?

options.A: Cornea
options.B: Retina
options.C: Sclera
options.D: Choroid

explanation: The cornea is the transparent front window of the eye that bends and admits light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of direct-acting relaxants like mebeverine over anticholinergics?

options.A: They can only be given safely through an intravenous drip
options.B: They work within seconds of entering the bloodstream
